Definition: from G473 and G3928; to go along opposite:--pass by on the other side.
BiblicalUsage: The priest and the Levite pass by on the other side of the wounded man on the road to Jericho, and the Samaritan stops. The word is the walk that keeps its distance, going along the far side of the road.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for passing by on the other side carries no doctrine of its own; its shame is the parable's, that the priest and the Levite saw the wounded man and kept to the far side.
